title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics - Nature Energy
gist: KAUST-led researchers (Stefaan De Wolf group) propose 'lattice compliance', a perovskite crystal's ability to elastically absorb stress, as the descriptor of photothermal stability for bromide-lean ~1.55 eV absorbers in bifacial perovskite/silicon tandems. Their devices reach 36.2 mW cm-2 power-generation density at 0.20 albedo and keep 90% of initial efficiency after more than 1,000 h of ISOS-L-2 testing at 65 °C.

insights.claim: Bifacial monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells reached a power-generation density of 36.2 mW cm-2 under 0.20 albedo-equivalent illumination.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Counting rear-side light, 36.2 mW/cm2 exceeds what front-only tandem efficiency figures suggest, which helps the case for utility-scale bifacial tandems.
insights.quote: bifacial monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems achieved a power-generation density of 36.2 mW cm−2 under 0.20 albedo-equivalent illumination

insights.claim: The tandems retained 90% of initial efficiency after more than 1,000 hours of ISOS-L-2 testing (1-sun illumination at 65 °C).
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: 1,000 h at 65 °C is progress but still far from the multi-decade field life needed for bankability.
insights.quote: retained 90% of their initial efficiency after over 1,000 h of ISOS-L-2 testing (1-sun at 65 °C)

insights.claim: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandems are framed as a promising route to high power output per unit area.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Area-normalized output matters most where land, racking and BOS costs dominate.
insights.quote: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells offer a promising route to high area-normalized power output.

insights.claim: Using ~1.55 eV perovskite absorbers in bifacial tandems reduces reliance on bromide, which largely mitigates light-induced halide segregation and moves the main stability challenge to the intrinsic photothermal resilience of bromide-lean absorbers.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Bifacial designs change which degradation mode matters, so stability R&D should focus on heat plus light rather than halide segregation.
insights.quote: Using ~1.55 eV perovskite absorbers reduces reliance on bromide, largely mitigating light-induced halide segregation and shifting the dominant stability challenge to the intrinsic photothermal resilience of bromide-lean absorbers.

insights.claim: Across the compositions studied, higher lattice compliance improves photothermal stability by suppressing thermally induced microstrain buildup, shifting deep-level defects toward shallower states, and reducing band-edge energetic disorder.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Gives a mechanistic reason why some perovskite compositions survive heat while others do not.
insights.quote: higher lattice compliance promotes photothermal stability by suppressing thermally induced microstrain accumulation, shifting deep-level defects towards shallower states and reducing band-edge energetic disorder

insights.claim: The authors propose lattice compliance, the ability of a crystal lattice to elastically accommodate stress, as a physically testable materials descriptor for designing stable perovskite absorbers.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A screenable descriptor could speed composition selection for commercial tandem developers, but it has only been shown across the compositions studied.
insights.quote: These results establish lattice compliance as a physically testable framework for designing stable perovskite absorbers.

insights.claim: The work was led by KAUST (Stefaan De Wolf, Fuzong Xu) with Soochow University, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Marmara University, funded partly by KAUST's Office of Sponsored Research and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
